title: Eiffel Tower
blurb: The Eiffel Tower is a 330 m wrought iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, built for the 1889 Exposition Universelle. This detailed model breaks the tower into 145 named components across 11 systems, from the compressed-air caissons under the Seine-side legs and the four decorative arches, through the lattice panels, elevators, and staircases, to the summit with Gustave Eiffel's apartment, the restaurants on the first two floors, the 72 engraved names, and the broadcasting aerial that lifts the tip to 330 m.

sourceUrls.label: List of names on the Eiffel Tower, Wikipedia

systems.name: Foundations
systems.description: Concrete footings, foundation slabs, compressed-air caissons, and anchor bolts. The east and south legs rest on 2 m slabs; the north and west legs, closer to the Seine, sit on 6 m slabs over caissons driven 22 m deep.

systems.name: Legs
systems.description: Four lattice girders that stand apart at the base and converge toward the top, carrying the tower. The metal structure weighs 7,300 tonnes out of 10,100 tonnes total.

systems.name: Lattice ironwork
systems.description: Cross-braced iron panels joining the legs on all four faces, tied by truss rings at each platform level. The finished tower joins 18,038 iron pieces with 2.5 million rivets.

systems.name: Platforms
systems.description: The three visitor levels at 57, 115, and 276 m, carried on iron support girders with railings. The first floor holds a glass floor section.

systems.name: Arches
systems.description: Four decorative arches spanning between the legs at the base, added by architect Stephen Sauvestre, each with a keystone and spandrel ornament.

systems.name: Elevators
systems.description: Lift shafts inside the legs with cars and counterweights, plus schematic hydraulic machinery. Eight elevators serve the tower.

systems.name: Stairs
systems.description: Staircase flights and landings connecting the ground to the upper levels. The full climb to the summit is 1,665 steps.

systems.name: Crown
systems.description: The summit at 276 m: the pavilion, Gustave Eiffel's private apartment, and the broadcasting aerial that brings the tip to 330 m.

systems.name: Hospitality
systems.description: Restaurants and visitor facilities: 58 Tour Eiffel on the first floor, Le Jules Verne on the second, a champagne bar at the summit, and ticket pavilions at the ground.

systems.name: Illumination
systems.description: Night lighting: sparkling light strings, the ring of floodlight projectors, and aviation warning strobes on the mast.

systems.name: Inscriptions
systems.description: The 72 names of French scientists, engineers, and mathematicians engraved on the frieze under the first balcony.

explanations.summit pavilion: Pavilion structures on the summit deck, 276 m above the ground.
explanations.eiffel apartment: A private apartment Gustave Eiffel built for himself on the third level, decorated with furniture by Jean Lachaise. It now holds wax figures of Eiffel, his daughter Claire, and Thomas Edison, with the phonograph Edison gave Eiffel as a gift.

explanations.tip beacon: Light assembly at the tip of the antenna. The tower was the tallest structure in the world from 1889 until the Chrysler Building was finished in 1930.
